native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: Diversity in Pottery Form collapsed while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased simultaneously during the 1800–1700 BCE century interval (the 18th century BCE leading into the 1700 BCE / 17th century BCE Late Neolithic horizon), marked by a ΔZ of -1.87 in form diversity down to its series floor of -1.13 and a concurrent ΔZ of +1.45 in decorative diversity up to +0.97.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Extracted and normalized pottery form and decoration z-scores across both capital.csv and time_series_data.csv. 2. Computed chronological forward-in-time first differences (ΔZ) across all 100-year century steps from 4300 BCE to 500 BCE. 3. Screened for instances of simultaneous negative ΔZ in form and positive ΔZ in decoration. 4. Confirmed uniqueness of the 1800–1700 BCE bin and synthesized contextual evidence from demographic and material capital indicators.

sub_hypo.text: During 1800–1700 BCE, pottery form diversity collapsed by ΔZ = -1.87 to its series floor of -1.13, while pottery decoration diversity simultaneously increased by ΔZ = +1.45 to +0.97. This interval was the unique century step exhibiting simultaneous declining form diversity and increasing decoration diversity among the 100-year steps from 4300 BCE to 500 BCE.
sub_hypo.context: The 1800–1700 BCE century interval, leading into the 1700 BCE / 17th century BCE Late Neolithic horizon, assessed using normalized pottery z-scores from capital.csv and time_series_data.csv.
sub_hypo.relations: Simultaneous opposite-direction changes in chronological forward-in-time first differences: pottery form diversity decreased by 1.87 Z units to its series minimum of -1.13, while pottery decoration diversity increased by 1.45 Z units to +0.97. This negative-form/positive-decoration combination was unique to 1800–1700 BCE across the screened 100-year steps from 4300 BCE to 500 BCE.
